rv.q: Warner’s “Onegin” never quite convinces — it’s coherent, occasionally persuasive, but ultimately negligible.

It didn't help, of course, that her Onegin (baritone Iurii Samoilov) didn't seem properly world-weary, or compelling enough to make her forget everything else in her life, despite his attractive vocal instrument. He made up for it in the final duet with Tatiana.
The Lithuanian soprano’s Tatiana did not disappoint as she limned a searing portrait of a woman moving from embarrassed yearning to stoic resignation caused by her doomed love for Onegin.

The chief attraction in this revival was Asmik Grigorian in her Met role debut as Tatiana. The Lithuanian soprano met all expectations in a riveting performance in which Grigorian’s vaunted dramatic skills were fully evident. Her Tatiana was carefully conceived and sculpted, yet always fresh and spontaneous vocally and dramatically.
On the whole, this might have been the most disappointing evening I have experience at the Met Opera this season.

cn.t: Warner's production disappoints as a lackluster replacement for the beloved Carsen staging, with critics finding it frustratingly lacking in intimacy despite solid casting and occasional vocal highlights.
